lines.text: You practise a speech and record it.
It sounds a little off, but you cannot say where.
Too fast? A pause in the wrong place? Too quiet at the end?
Contrastive Voice shows you which words to fix, and how.
Give it two readings of the same text: yours, and a reference you want to sound like.
It lines them up word by word.
Then it marks each place where your delivery departs from the reference.
Pace, pauses, pitch, emphasis, volume and clarity, pinned to the exact words and times.
Every finding comes with a concrete fix.
Here is an example from the gallery.
The reference is Ronald Reagan's farewell address from 1989.
lines.spoken: The reference is Ronald Reagan's farewell address, from nineteen eighty-nine.

lines.text: The other reading is a copy of that recording with four delivery edits added.
The biggest fixes come first: rushed words, a fade, and a dropped pause.
The score is 86 out of 100, measured against the reference.
lines.spoken: The score is eighty-six out of a hundred, measured against the reference.

lines.text: Now listen to the edited reading while the transcript follows along.
The pause after 'morning' is gone, the monument phrase is rushed, and the last words fade.
lines.spoken: The pause after morning is gone, the monument phrase is rushed, and the last words fade.

lines.text: Each highlight sits on the words where you heard the problem.
Click a flag to open its finding.
It shows both measured values and the threshold.
Here, five words took 0.87 s. In the reference they take 1.62 s.
lines.spoken: Here, five words took point eight seven seconds. In the reference, they take one point six two seconds.

lines.text: The fix: give these words about 1.6 s, and lengthen the stressed words rather than adding gaps.
lines.spoken: The fix: give these words about one point six seconds, and lengthen the stressed words, rather than adding gaps.

lines.text: Added after the frozen evaluation: 'Hear it fixed' edits your own recording toward the reference.
lines.spoken: Added after the frozen evaluation: Hear it fixed, edits your own recording toward the reference.

lines.text: Listen to yours, the edited take, then the target.
Still flagged, partly changed: the score rises 3.07 points.
lines.spoken: Still flagged, partly changed. The score rises three point zero seven points.

lines.text: It is an edited preview of the change, not a guarantee.

clip.caption: Yours, edited, then the target: 'over the grounds here to the Washington Monument and then the Mall'

lines.text: 'Fix everything and listen' edits the whole reading: 86.11 becomes 96.17.
lines.spoken: Fix everything and listen, edits the whole reading. Eighty-six point one one becomes ninety-six point one seven.

lines.text: The list says what each fix did: two spots are no longer flagged, three are still flagged.
A clean reading should get no flags: the identity example scores 100, with nothing flagged.
lines.spoken: A clean reading should get no flags. The identity example scores a hundred, with nothing flagged.

lines.text: To check your own speech, upload your reading and a reference reading of the same text.
Also added after the evaluation: with no reference, the reading is graded against itself, and three spots stand out.
That is a rough check. A reference reading of the same text gives better results.
How does it work?
Forced alignment times every word in both recordings, at 20 ms resolution.
lines.spoken: Forced alignment times every word in both recordings, at twenty millisecond resolution.

lines.text: Nine delivery measures are taken on the same words in both, over five-word windows.
Volume and pitch are relative to your own median, so a deep voice is not a flaw.
Only a difference past a threshold fitted on flawless comparisons is flagged.
2,410 audio files: nine public-domain speeches, with edits of known type, place and size.
lines.spoken: Two thousand, four hundred and ten audio files: nine public-domain speeches, with edits of known type, place and size.

lines.text: On held-out speakers, F1 is 0.812 as pre-registered; 0.879 with one detection per change.
lines.spoken: On held-out speakers, F one is point eight one two as pre-registered. Point eight seven nine, with one detection per change.

lines.text: Zero false flags in 5.89 minutes of unedited and placebo copies.
lines.spoken: Zero false flags, in five point eight nine minutes of unedited and placebo copies.

lines.text: Gain and MP3 keep every detection; 10 dB babble keeps 60 %.
lines.spoken: Gain and M P three keep every detection. Ten decibel babble keeps sixty percent.

lines.text: Run it yourself with one Docker command.
Open the page in your browser, then try the examples or your own reading.
The detector is on Hugging Face, and the code is on GitHub.
Record. Compare. Fix the exact words.
Contrastive Voice.
